object_description: two loosely related buildings framing a large open setting
design_condition: The buildings are placed loosely across the plot to maximize open space, with the northern building following the topography and the kindergarten positioned along the district street.

positive.statement: The chosen setting generates maximum open spaces.
The northern building derives its development layout from the topography and separates the different functions in an interesting way.
The hard court is convincingly framed by the edge of the slope.
The kindergarten building is convincingly organized, with three entrances linked by an internal access.
The teaching and group rooms are well proportioned and have sufficient light.
The covered outdoor spaces provide an additional spatial quality.
Placing the kindergarten building directly on the district street allows generous free outdoor play space.

negative.statement: The potential of the generated outdoor spaces is not exploited, and the parking arrangement is particularly unconvincing.
The kindergarten and existing school form a loose unity, while the complex lacks spatial cohesion.
The three school buildings hardly seem to relate to one another.
The decentralized arrangement of classrooms and play areas is controversial.
The internal functional distribution has deficiencies, including the need for two offices serving the multi-purpose rooms.
The route from the kindergarten rooms through the cloakrooms to the outdoor play area is somewhat complicated.
The buildings have little in common in appearance, and the project lacks an overall spatial and functional idea.
